turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Dr. Smith. I came in because, well, since I tried to clean up my image and my daily routine for some arts board stuff I'm involved with, I’ve been a lot more tense and down than I expected to be. 

I'm still doing the basics, but I just keep dropping little things that I normally really care about—like my fair planning notes or my design drafts. And then I just feel guilty about falling behind, and I end up canceling plans with people instead of actually catching up on the work. It's just been bothering me, so I figured I should talk to someone.

symptom_reasoning.S081: The patient reports developing emotional and behavioral difficulties, including feeling tense and down and withdrawing socially, in direct response to the stressor of adjusting their routine and image for an arts board.

turns.doctor_question: How long have you been feeling this way—tense, down, and having trouble keeping up with things?
turns.patient_response: It's been about two months now. Pretty much ever since I started trying to overhaul my routine and my presentation.

turns.doctor_question: Over these past two months, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, even ones unrelated to your current stress?
turns.patient_response: Not really, no. I still like the things I usually enjoy. It's more just that... I end up not doing them because I feel guilty about being behind on my other work. But if I actually let myself sit down and, you know, watch a show or do a hobby that isn't related to the arts board, I still get the same enjoyment out of it. I just haven't been letting myself do those things as much lately.

symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient explicitly denies a loss of interest or pleasure, stating they still enjoy their hobbies and get the same enjoyment out of them when they engage in them.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself worrying excessively about various things in your life—like health, finances, or relationships—or does your anxiety mainly center around the arts board work and falling behind?
turns.patient_response: No, I wouldn't say I worry excessively about everything else. I mean, my health and finances are fine, and my relationships are okay, even though I've been canceling on people. It's really just focused on the arts board stuff and how I'm falling behind on my notes and drafts. That's what makes me tense.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient explicitly denies worrying excessively across multiple life domains such as health, finances, and relationships, stating their concern is limited to their arts board work.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from feeling tense or stressed about the arts board work, have you noticed feeling sad, down, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, over these past two months?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. I mean, I don't feel hopeless or sad all day. It's... it's really just the stress of the work. I get frustrated with myself because I know I'm behind, but I wouldn't say I feel down most of the time. It's mostly just that tense feeling when I think about everything I still need to get done.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly denies feeling sad all day or feeling down most of the time.
symptom_reasoning.S083: The patient explicitly states that they do not feel hopeless.

turns.doctor_question: When you feel tense about falling behind, do you also notice physical signs of anxiety—like a racing heart, restlessness, or muscle tension—that stand out as the main way this stress shows up for you?
turns.patient_response: Um, no, I haven't noticed anything like a racing heart. I guess my shoulders might get a little tight sometimes, but... I think that's mostly just from sitting at my desk trying to force myself to work. So, no, it doesn't really show up as a big physical thing for me. It's really just that mental stress of knowing I'm behind.

symptom_reasoning.S061: The patient denies experiencing muscle tension as a physical symptom of anxiety, clarifying that minor shoulder tightness is merely due to desk posture and not a significant physical manifestation of stress.
